A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UltraViCo work. The complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D support reliable comparison despite repagination and figure relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-generation evaluations, a user study, attention analyses, ablations, and runtime measurements in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the benchmark comparisons, user rankings, ablations, and efficiency measurements.

M1.justification: The attention-logit decay procedure, targeted suppression at harmonic positions, and efficient attention implementation are unchanged. Equations (5)–(6), Algorithm 1, and the model-specific adaptations in Appendix C.2 are retained.

E1.justification: Both retain VBench evaluation and the same video extrapolation, controllable generation, video editing, pose-guided generation, and long-video continuation scenarios. Appendix examples remain present despite relocation.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and 3 retain PE, PI, NTK, YaRN, TASR, and RIFLEx. Table 2 retains Sliding Window, FreeNoise, and FIFO-Diffusion with and without UltraViCo. The newly cited works are not added to the experimental comparisons.

E3.justification: The base models, extrapolation settings, metrics, and hyperparameters are unchanged. Both retain the 100-prompt main evaluation, 25-prompt supplementary evaluation, and user study with 10 participants and 10 prompts (Section 4.1 and Appendix C).

E4.justification: Both contain the same attention-masking interventions, attention-concentration comparisons in Appendix B.7, decay-strategy ablations, and alpha/beta sensitivity analyses in Appendix D.2. Renumbering and relocating figures adds no analysis.

E5.justification: The attention-logit means and standard deviations across layers, heads, and query positions remain unchanged in Appendices B.3–B.4. Neither version supplies repeated-run counts, seed variation, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the benchmark comparisons.

E6.justification: Tables 1–8 retain the same result entries and numerical values. For example, UltraViCo on HunyuanVideo at 4× extrapolation remains at Dynamic Degree 42 and Imaging Quality 66.54 in Table 1. Plotted results and qualitative examples also match after relocation.

T1.justification: Proposition 1, its proof in Appendix B.5, the periodic-output and statistical-attention derivations, and the associated assumptions and mathematical definitions are unchanged.

C1.justification: Both retain the claims that attention dispersion unifies the two extrapolation failures, that training-free attention concentration addresses them, and that UltraViCo extends practical extrapolation from 2× to 4× while supporting downstream tasks. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same scientific scope.

C2.justification: The interpretations of harmonic periodicity and attention dispersion, the consistency-versus-decay tradeoffs, and the first-frame VAE hypothesis in Appendix C.2 are retained. No substantive applicability qualification or limitation is added or removed.

D1.justification: v2 removes v1’s standalone Reproducibility Statement saying that code and prompts are included in supplementary material. The project-page link, Figure 1’s supplementary prompt/video reference, Appendix C.2’s metric-code reference, and implementation details remain. This changes disclosure without establishing any withdrawal of resources.

R1.justification: v2 adds six cited works: Radial Attention in Section 2, three Ma et al. works on controllable generation, and two Yan et al. works on masked autoregressive models in Appendix A. These modestly broaden the background; the positioning relative to RIFLEx and other long-video methods is unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 updates the publication header and author footnotes, adds acknowledgements, removes the standalone reproducibility section, and lightly edits citation punctuation and related-work wording. The scientific narrative and section organization remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: The segment-wise continuation example moves from Figure 9 on v1 page 10 to Figure 18 on v2 page 27. Other appendix figures are renumbered, and figures and tables are redistributed across pages. All 18 figures and eight tables retain their substantive visual content and structure.

improvement.justification: The method, proofs, experimental evidence, and conclusions remain unchanged. Added citations and editorial cleanup provide limited benefits, while removing the standalone reproducibility statement reduces the prominence of access information. Because implementation details, supplementary references, and the project-page link remain, these edits do not materially alter the paper’s overall scientific support or reproducibility.
